*Sanidassanattika, Dassanahetuttika* (Patthana 23.47) is an Abhidhamma text belonging to the Paṭṭhāna section of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Structurally, it represents a combinatorial matrix text that synthesizes two triads (*ttika*): the visible/with-reaction triad (*sanidassanattika*) and the triad concerning roots abandoned by vision (*dassanahetuttika*), analyzing their conditional relationships in accordance with the standard conditional methodology of the Paṭṭhāna [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
No direct parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan traditions are recorded in SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language matches meeting the scoring threshold [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated textual reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive internal reuse within the Paṭṭhāna collection, identifying 164 matching passages across 37 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest textual alignments occur with other treatments incorporating the *sanidassanattika* or *dassanahetuttika* matrices, notably *Sanidassanattika, Dassanenapahātabbadukādi* (Patthana 22.35; 26 matches), *Sanidassanattika, Mahantaraduka* (Patthana 22.32; 19 matches), and *Sanidassanattika, Āsavagocchaka* (Patthana 22.30; 10 matches) [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits high segment similarity with adjacent triplet sections such as *Sanidassanattika, Dassanattika* (Patthana 23.46) and parallel pairings like *Kusalattika, Dassanahetuttika* (Patthana 23.8) [DharmaNexus].
